title: Chapter 104: Hensheng: To Hate Life 7
content:
Chapter 104

Su She realized his mistake a second too late, hastily yanking his lapels shut. But it was no use—the men facing him had already caught an eyeful of his exposed chest. Clustered tight over the skin near his heart were more than a dozen grotesque, pitch-black craters of varying sizes.

The unmistakable signature of the Hundred Holes Curse.

Worse, this was definitively not the mark of someone who had fallen victim to it. If he were the target, given how far those holes had spread, the rotting hollows would have eaten through his internal organs and core by now, completely severing his ability to wield spiritual power. Yet he had been freely burning through high-grade teleportation talismans that demanded massive reserves of energy. There was only one possible explanation: these marks were the backlash of a curse ricocheting onto the caster.

Back then, Wei Wuxian had tried everything to hunt down the true culprit to clear his own name. But finding one faceless stranger in a sea of millions had been impossible, and before long, the spiraling aftermath had escalated far beyond what catching a single saboteur could ever fix, so he’d given up hope. Who would have guessed that after scouring the earth to no avail, the answer would land right in his lap tonight without him lifting a finger?

Jin Ling was out of the loop, and Nie Huaisang probably hadn’t connected the dots either, but Lan Xichen was already turning a severe look toward Jin Guangyao. "Jin-zongzhu, was this part of the Qiongqi Path ambush, too?"

Jin Guangyao kept his tone neutral. "What makes you say that?"

"Is it not completely obvious?!" Jiang Cheng sneered, his voice dripping with ice. "If Jin Zixun hadn't been cursed in the first place, none of that shit would have ever happened! That single ambush took out both Jin Zixuan and Jin Zixun, wiping out every generational rival in one clean sweep and bulldozing your path to the Clan Leader's seat and the Chief Cultivator's throne! Su She cast that curse, and he's your pet lapdog. Does anyone seriously need to ask who pulled his strings?!"

Jin Guangyao neither confirmed nor denied it, looking as though he were entirely focused on regulating his breath.

Wei Wuxian was so furious he broke into a dark chuckle. Glaring at Su She, he demanded, "Did I ever cross you? I had zero bad blood with you! Hell, I barely even knew you!"

Jin Guangyao murmured, "Wei-gongzi, shouldn't you know better than anyone? Does having no bad blood ever guarantee peace? Of course not. Nobody starts out with a grudge; someone always has to step up and throw the first blade."

"You vicious little snake!" Jiang Cheng spat through gritted teeth.

Su She, however, let out a venomous scoff. "Get over yourself! Who said I cursed Jin Zixun just to frame you? I wasn't even serving under the Sect Leader back then! I cursed that bastard simply because I wanted to!"

Wei Wuxian’s eyes narrowed. "So you had beef with Jin Zixun?"

"Arrogant bastards who look down their noses at everyone?" Su She hissed. "I kill every single one I see!"

Wei Wuxian didn’t need three guesses to know who held the number one spot on Su She's list of 'arrogant bastards.' Unable to hold back, he snapped, "What is your problem with Hanguang-jun, anyway? How the hell has he ever looked down on you?!"

"Are you blind?!" Su She fired back, spitting mad. "If Lan Wangji hadn't won the reincarnation lottery and landed in a prestigious clan, what right would he have to act so high and mighty?! And why does everyone always claim I'm copying him?! The whole world trips over themselves singing praises for his pristine, untouchable virtue—the grand Hanguang-jun, a paragon of righteousness so immaculate that he's tangled up in filthy, sordid depravity with the irredeemably wicked, universally despised Yiling Laozu?! What a fucking joke!"

Wei Wuxian opened his mouth to tear into him, but a sudden flash of memory stopped him cold. That bitter, venomous glare looked intimately familiar. He’d seen it somewhere before.

The realization hit him like a thunderclap.

"It was you!"

Caiyi Town. Biling Lake. The Waterborne Abyss. A sword slipping into the depths. The cave of the Xuanwu of Slaughter, and the disciple who’d shoved Mianmian forward as live bait—Su She!

Wei Wuxian suddenly burst into loud, uproarious laughter.

"I get it now," he said, shaking his head.

Lan Wangji looked at him. "Understand what?"

Wei Wuxian just kept shaking his head, a hollow smile playing on his lips.

He knew exactly what kind of man Jin Zixun had been. The guy had treated disciples from subsidiary sects like dirt beneath his boots, viewing them as glorified domestic servants and considering it an insult to his noble blood just to sit at the same banquet table. And Su She, hailing from a minor offshoot clan under Lanling Jin's thumb, had inevitably been forced to attend banquets at Koi Tower, crossing paths with Jin Zixun time and time again. One was an insecure, hyper-defensive prick looking for slights, and the other was an overbearing, arrogant bully. It was no surprise at all that some petty clash had pushed Su She to nurse a lethal grudge.

If that was the truth, then the whole catalyst behind Jin Zixun catching the Hundred Holes Curse had absolutely nothing to do with him. Yet in the end, he had been the one saddled with the bloody blame.

The entire tragedy at the Qiongqi Path had ignited solely because Jin Zixun was cursed. Without that spark, the Lanling Jin Clan would have had zero excuse to corner him. Wen Ning wouldn’t have lost control and gone on a slaughter spree. Wei Wuxian wouldn't have carried the crushing weight of Jin Zixuan's death on his soul. And none of the dominoes that followed would have ever fallen.

And now, after all these years, he was finding out that the killer hadn't even set the trap to frame him. The entire catastrophe hadn't started because of him at all!

That truth was a thousand times harder to swallow.

The laughter died in Wei Wuxian's throat, leaving his eyes burning scarlet with a mix of caustic irony and bitter self-mockery. "To think it all came down to a piece of work like you... Over a petty, pointless grudge like that!"

Jin Guangyao seemed to pluck the thoughts right out of his head. "Wei-gongzi, you really shouldn't look at it that way."

Wei Wuxian raised a cold brow. "Oh? You know what I'm thinking?"

"Naturally, it's hardly a mystery," Jin Guangyao replied effortlessly. "You're sitting there thinking how unfair it all was. But the truth is, there was no injustice. Even if Su She hadn't cursed Jin Zixun, you would have ended up besieged and put down sooner or later for a completely different reason."

He flashed a smooth, gentle smile. "Because that’s simply who you are. Put politely, you're chivalrous, bold, and untamed; put bluntly, you go around stepping on toes wherever you walk. Unless every single person you've ever offended lives a charmed, accident-free life, the second anything goes sideways or someone trips them up, you will always be the very first suspect on their minds, and the very first target for their revenge. And that is a variable completely beyond your control."

Wei Wuxian let out a dry chuckle. "Look at that. I hate that you actually make sense."

Jin Guangyao continued, "Besides, even if you hadn't lost your grip back at Qiongqi Path, could you honestly guarantee you'd keep control for the rest of your days? People like you are simply built to die young. See? Doesn't looking at it like that make you feel much better?"

"You're the one who's going to die young, you bastard!" Jiang Cheng roared.

Disregarding his ruptured chest wound, Jiang Cheng lunged forward with Sandu drawn, only for fresh blood to violently burst through his bandages. Jin Ling scrambled to tackle him back down. Pinned and half-blind with rage, Jiang Cheng snarled, "You son of a whore! You’d throw away every scrap of dignity just to claw your way up the ladder! You expect us to believe you didn't order Su She to do it?! Who the hell are you trying to fool?!"

At the wordsson of a whore, the pleasant smile on Jin Guangyao's face hitched for a fraction of a second.

He looked toward Jiang Cheng, letting the silence hang before offering a cool, measured retort: "Jiang-zongzhu, collect yourself. I understand why you're lashing out. The only reason your temper is flaring like this is because finding out the truth about that golden core has cracked your precious pride, leaving you nursing a bitter drop of guilt. You're desperate to pin Wei-gongzi's past downfall onto a convenient villain—a monster you can blame for everything so you can rally the mob, tear him apart, avenge your martial brother, and shave a little weight off your own guilty conscience.

"If convincing yourself that I personally engineered everything from the Hundred Holes Curse to the slaughter at Qiongqi Path helps you sleep at night, then by all means, indulge your fantasy. But you need to look in the mirror and understand that you played a massive part in driving Wei-gongzi into his grave. Why did the sects unite so easily to bring down the Yiling Laozu? Why did every bystander and their dog jump at the chance to scream for his head? Why was the realm so overwhelmingly eager to beat him down? Was it truly just pure righteousness at work? Of course not. A generous portion of the blame lies squarely on your shoulders."

Jiang Cheng scoffed coldly. Sensing the venomous mind games ramping up, Lan Xichen barked a low warning: "Jin-zongzhu!"

Jin Guangyao didn't bat an eye, continuing with conversational ease: "...Back then, the Lanling Jin, Qinghe Nie, and Gusu Lan clans were locking horns, carving up the lion's share of the realm and leaving the smaller clans scrambling for table scraps. And right there sat you, having just rebuilt Lotus Pier from the ashes, backed by an impossibly dangerous, unpredictable wildcard like the Yiling Laozu, Wei Wuxian. Did you honestly think the other clans were thrilled to watch a young sect leader sit pretty with that kind of unmatched leverage?

"Fortunately for them, the rift between you and your shixiong was an open secret. Everyone smelled blood in the water. Naturally, they stoked the flames every chance they got to drive you two apart—after all, keeping the Yunmeng Jiang Clan down was the easiest way to keep their own houses safe. Jiang-zongzhu, if you had shown just an ounce more warmth toward your shixiong back then, presenting an unshakeable, united front to make the meddlers back off, or if you had shown a shred of grace after things went south, the story would never have ended in blood. Ah, come to think of it, weren't you the vanguard leading the charge during the First Siege of the Burial Mounds...?"

Wei Wuxian cut in, voice flat: "Seems 'whore's son' really is your sore spot, Jin-zongzhu. No wonder you couldn't resist butchering Chifeng-zun."

At the mention of Nie Mingjue, the air around Lan Xichen darkened. Jin Guangyao's smile stiffened once more, and he smoothly pushed himself to his feet.

He had finished circulating his spiritual energy. Flexing his left fingers, he found the mobility fully restored and immediately barked, "Rally the men. We move out."

"Yes, sir!" Su She replied.

Two monks stepped up to bracket Lan Xichen, moving to heave the heavy temple doors open, when Jin Guangyao suddenly paused. "Almost slipped my mind."

He turned back toward Lan Xichen. "If I'm not mistaken, Zewu-jun's sealed spiritual meridians should be loosening up right about now."

Given how vastly Lan Xichen outclassed him in raw cultivation, keeping his core locked required Jin Guangyao to reapply the suppression seal every two hours, or the elder would break free through sheer spiritual force. He closed the distance, offering a shallow bow. "Pardon the offense."

Just as his hand reached out, a heavy, pale mass slammed down from the rafters with a wet thud right before his boots. Jin Guangyao sprang back on pure reflex, his eyes going wide as he took in the pale, sprawling flesh on the floorboards.

It was a stark-naked woman.

She lay prone, face pressed against the stone, her limbs contorting and twisting in unnatural, sickening angles as she dragged herself toward Jin Guangyao. Su She struck with his sword in a flash, running her through; the woman let out a piercing shriek as flames abruptly erupted across her flesh. Hauling herself upright, she staggered through the inferno, clawing toward Jin Guangyao with scorched, blackened hands, her eyes burning with pure, unadulterated malice. Su She cleaved through her with a second strike, scattering the fiery corpse into smoke and ash.

Jin Guangyao stumbled back a couple of paces, his heel catching on something soft. Looking down, he found two tangled bodies writhing on the tiles, a rotting hand shooting out to clamp iron-tight around his ankle.

From across the hall, a sharp whistle pierced through the damp gloom.

Su She’s jaw clenched with pure venom: "Wei Wuxian!"

Without anyone noticing, the towering Guanyin statue had been painted with a sprawling, chaotic array of fresh blood runes.

The focal point of the temple's suppression array was anchored right within this very sanctuary. With Wei Wuxian quietly shattering the core of the seal while their attention had been elsewhere, whatever dark horrors had been pinned beneath the earth were now tearing their way to the surface in a relentless, pouring tide!

Suddenly, Jin Ling let out a panicked yelp: "What the hell?!"

Jiang Cheng was furiously swatting at the boy’s clothes with both hands—the hem of Jin Ling’s golden robes had spontaneously caught fire! Jin Ling had gotten off light; several monks were already engulfed in wild, dancing flames, shrieking as they rolled frantically across the floorboards.

Su She and Jin Guangyao knew the blood runes on the Guanyin statue had to be wiped clean immediately, but their boots were completely hemmed in by screaming, burning disciples and an endless swarm of naked, writhing ghouls. The phantoms obeyed Wei Wuxian’s mental commands, pointedly steering clear of Jiang Cheng and Jin Ling, but Jin Ling still held Suihua defensively before his chest, stammering, "What kind of monsters are these?! I've never seen anything so..."

So brazenly lewd and utterly depraved!

Jin Guangyao's eyes burned with furious heat. Releasing a concussive blast from his palm, the flames detonated, clearing a narrow path for him to dash toward the altar. But just as his hand reached up to smear the blood runes away, an icy chill kissed the small of his back.

Lan Xichen’s voice dropped low and dangerous behind his shoulder: "Don't move."

Jin Guangyao moved to twist away and counter, but Lan Xichen brought a heavy palm strike crashing down against his spine.

Jin Guangyao choked out, "Zewu-jun... You... You broke the seal."

Before Lan Xichen could offer a word, Su She’s spiritual blade, Nanping, slashed through the chaos, driving straight for Wei Wuxian's throat.

Clang!

A blinding arc of familiar, azure sword-glare intercepted the strike with pristine, crystalline fury.

Bichen!

The blades collided with an ear-splitting crack—and Nanping snapped clean in two!

The violent backlash tore open the webbing of Su She’s thumb, blood spraying across his robes as the bones in his forearm popped and rattled from the impact. The broken hilt clattered against the stone tiles. Clamping his left hand over his mangled right arm, Su She went the color of a fresh corpse.

Lan Wangji held Bichen in one hand, his free arm hooking smooth and firm around Wei Wuxian’s waist, effortlessly pulling him behind his back into his guard. Wei Wuxian had zero need for a human shield, but he thoroughly enjoyed the pampering, leaning happily against that broad, sturdy chest.

The entire upheaval had detonated in the span of a few heartbeats. By the time the Lanling Jin cultivators snapped to their senses, Su She was clutching a shattered, bleeding arm with his chest wound torn wide open, and the razor-sharp edge of Bichen was resting dead-center against Jin Guangyao’s throat.

With their leader completely pinned, the entire garrison froze, paralyzed with fear.

Lan Xichen opened his mouth to take control of the room, but everyone's expressions suddenly twisted in profound, uncomfortable disgust. Lan Xichen cleared his throat, averting his gaze. "Master Wei... Would you mind... Dispersing these spirits first?"

The writhing apparitions weren't just stark naked, thoroughly indecent, and making a mockery of public decorum—they were letting out deeply compromising, breathless moans that left zero room to question what they were doing. None of the cultivators had ever laid eyes on such an overtly pornographic haunting. Lan Xichen turned his face away entirely, Jiang Cheng looked like he’d swallowed a toad, and Jin Ling's cheeks were cycling rapidly between bright red and mortified white.

Wei Wuxian glanced at Lan Wangji beside him, suddenly realizing that forcing a man who used to get flustered and furious over erotic art in his youth to watch this live show was entirely uncalled for.

He offered an embarrassed, defensive shrug: "Look, my only goal was to pop whatever curse he had buried under the floor to buy us some time. How the hell was I supposed to know this was the brand of horror he had locked away?!"

Lan Wangji spared the writhing spirits only a fleeting, clinical glance before looking away alongside his brother. He offered two quiet, measured words:

"A fire."

Wei Wuxian nodded vigorously, instantly putting on an air of utmost scholarly gravity. "Exactly. These vengeful spirits all burned to death. Looks like a massive inferno consumed this land in the past, taking a lot of lives with it. And to cover up the tragedy and pin down the furious resentful energy born from the blaze, Jin-zongzhu personally commissioned a grand Guanyin Temple right over the ashes."

Lan Xichen turned his eyes toward the captive. "Jin-zongzhu, was this fire your doing?"

Jiang Cheng scoffed, voice dripping with cold disgust: "Those vengeful spirits are trying to tear him limb from limb. Is there even a shred of doubt that he lit the match?!"
